newsitem.title: CHINA: Rockwell hopes to supply China avionics.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell hopes to supply China avionics.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp hopes the company will become the supplier of avionics for the 100-seater airliner to be developed by China, Singapore and a European consortium, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Rockwell's turnover would hit $8.0 billion this year, of which about 15 percent would come from the Asia-Pacific region. Xinhua quoted Donald R. Beall, chairman and chief executive officer of the industrial and electronics firm, as saying.
Its sales in the region were projected to double to about $2.0 billion by 2001, while sales of its electronic products in China would reach $200 million by 2001, he said.
Rockwell has invested about $50 million in China and set up four joint ventures, primarily in the automotive industry.
Rockwell was working with Aviation Industries of China (AVIC) to develop avionics for the proposed regional 100-seat airliner, he said.
"While the decision process continues, we will work aggressively to maximise our participation," Beall said.
The 100-seat airliner is to be built by AVIC with partners Aero International Asia, a wing of Airbus Industrie and Singapore Technologies Aerospace.
AVIC would hold 46 percent of the $2.1 billion venture, while Aero International Asia would take 39 percent and Singapore Technologies Aerospace 15 percent.
The venture is targeted to deliver its first airliner by the year 2001 and Chinese industry analysts have predicted world demand for 100-seat planes to reach 3,000 by 2020, state media has said.

Rockwell also hoped to sell its global positioning system (GPS) air traffic management system to China, Beall said, adding that its manufacturing plants in Shanghai might be involved in building the air traffic management systems in the future.
The company was interested in co-producing its air traffic alert and collision avoidance systems for aircraft with Chinese partners, Beall said.
Collins, a Rockwell subsidiary, has been providing avionics equipment for Chinese carriers for the past three decades.
